title: Perpetual Falls
short: Lay stone aqueducts that carry water uphill in an impossible optical illusion.
full:
Water always runs downhill. So how does it climb back to the top of the waterfall?

Perpetual Falls is a puzzle game built on an impossible illusion. From its fixed viewpoint, a step one storey down lines up exactly with the square in front of it, so a channel that looks level can carry water from the foot of a waterfall all the way back to its top. Lay stone aqueducts, lead every falling stream home, and set the mill wheels turning forever.

Close the loop and the camera swings off its angle to reveal the trick: the aqueduct really runs downhill, and the last step is several storeys straight up.

HOW IT PLAYS
• Drag from the pool at the foot of a tower to lay aqueducts, one stone at a time
• Lead the water back to the top of a tower and close every waterfall into one endless loop
• Straight channels can cross each other, and old fixed conduits pierce the walls
• Taller towers, more wheels and bigger levels as you go

FEATURES
• 50 levels, from a single tower to vast 20×20 waterworks with six towers and five-storey falls
• Endless levels after level 50: new levels built for you, and the same board for every player
• Realistic 3D stonework, moss and ivy, flowing water, turning mill wheels and spatial sound
• Earn up to three stars on every level: solve it without hints in the fewest stones
• Hints show the next piece when you're stuck, and a destination guide shows where each stream must arrive
• Save photos of your finished levels
• A Google Play Games leaderboard ranked by total stars, with each player's total time
• Day and night looks that follow your phone's theme
• Graphics quality adjusts automatically for your device; pinch to zoom on the biggest levels
• Plays offline, with no ads

FREE TO START
Levels 1 to 25 are free. One purchase of Endless levels unlocks levels 26 to 50 and the endless levels, with no ads and no subscription.

Made by 341 Games.
